```{python}
#| label: fig-moores-law
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Moore's law: the number of components per integrated circuit versus time. The blue points reproduce the data available to Moore in 1965; the dashed red line is his extrapolation of a doubling every year (data after Moore, 'Cramming more components onto integrated circuits,' Electronics, 1965)."

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# data points as published by Moore in 1965 (log2 of components vs. year)
years = np.array([1959, 1962, 1963, 1964, 1965])
components = np.array([1, 8, 16, 32, 64])

# extrapolation: doubling every year until 1975
years_ext = np.arange(1959, 1976)
components_ext = 2.0 ** (years_ext - 1959)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
ax.semilogy(years_ext, components_ext, 'r--', lw=1.5,
            label='Extrapolation (2$\\times$ per year)')
ax.semilogy(years, components, 'o', color='tab:blue', ms=6,
            label='Data (Moore, 1965)')

ax.set_xlabel('Year')
ax.set_ylabel('Components per integrated circuit')
ax.set_xlim(1958, 1976)
ax.grid(True, which='both', alpha=0.3)
ax.legend(loc='upper left')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
